1: # Minimal translation from accepted NL0
2: 
3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 300-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1, with E×[0,1]=F in the Euclidean space Eucl(n+1).

definitions.type: family, indexed by k∈ℕ, of Euclidean metric spaces
definitions.definition: Eucl(k)=ℝ^k, the real coordinate vectors indexed by {0,...,k−1}, with distance dist(x,y)=(∑_{j<k}(x_j−y_j)^2)^(1/2). Eucl(0) consists of the empty vector. On Eucl(k)×ℝ we use dist((x,t),(y,u))=(dist(x,y)^2+|t−u|^2)^(1/2), identified with Eucl(k+1) by appending the last coordinate; no maximum product metric is used. Balls mean {y:dist(x,y)<a}. All these spaces carry the topology of this metric and its Borel measurable structure.

binders.type: real coordinate vector of length k
real coordinate vector of length k
coordinate index bound by j<k in the finite sum

definitions.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric or extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a subset A of a metric or extended metric space X, diam(A)=sup{d(x,y):x,y∈A} in [0,∞], where d is its (extended) distance and sup∅=0. Thus diam∅=0. When diam(A)≤a<∞ we treat it as the corresponding finite nonnegative real number. Countable sums of nonnegative quantities mean the supremum of finite partial sums, and may be infinite; powers with positive exponent have 0^s=0 and ∞^s=∞.

definitions.type: Hausdorff content and measure functions on Euclidean sets with positive real exponent
definitions.definition: For every k∈ℕ, A⊆Eucl(k), s>0 and δ>0, H^s_δ(A)=inf{∑_{i≥0}(diam U_i)^s : (U_i) is a countable cover of A and diam U_i≤δ for every i}, and H^s(A)=sup_{δ>0} H^s_δ(A), with values in [0,∞]. Finite covers are allowed by padding with empty sets; empty members contribute zero. The infimum of an empty collection is ∞. This is exactly the unnormalized diameter-power convention of problem.md:34–42.

definitions.type: pair of native Hausdorff measure and dimension constructions on an extended metric space
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space X with its Borel measurable structure, Native(X).measure(σ) denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure σ, defined in the pinned library as Measure.mkMetric(r↦r^σ). Here mkMetric forms, for each positive extended radius, the covering outer measure with cost r^σ of the extended diameter for nonempty sets (empty sets cost zero), and takes their supremum as the radius decreases to zero, with the Borel measure structure. Evaluations on arbitrary sets mean outer measure evaluations, without requiring those sets measurable. Extended powers use the native ENNReal.rpow convention, including r^0=1. Native(X).dimension(A) denotes dimH A, defined as sup over a∈[0,∞) with Native(X).measure(a)(A)=∞ of the extended nonnegative number a; an empty supremum is zero. This names the exact native definitions, not an assertion about H.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: extended nonnegative Hausdorff dimension of Euclidean sets
definitions.definition: For k∈ℕ and A⊆Eucl(k), dim_H(A)=Native(Eucl(k)).dimension(A), the usual Hausdorff dimension, valued in [0,∞]. In particular the empty set has dimension zero by this definition. No finiteness is imposed by this definition; finiteness of the dimensions occurring in the target is proved below.

I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}. When I or a subset of the real line is an argument of H or dim_H, it is identified with the subset of Eucl(1) obtained by t↦(t), the one-coordinate vector; this map has distance sqrt((t−u)^2)=|t−u|. Thus all diameter, cover and dimension notation for real subsets uses exactly their usual real-line metric. In λ(I) and real integrals I is the real interval itself.
F=E×I={(x,t):x∈E,t∈I}, regarded as a subset of Eucl(n+1) under D001's coordinate-appending Euclidean isometry.
D=dim_H(E). Finiteness and 0≤D≤n are conclusions, not assumptions.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line, evaluated as an outer measure on arbitrary sets
definitions.definition: λ is the usual Lebesgue measure MeasureTheory.volume on ℝ. For any nonnegative extended-real function f, ∫f dλ denotes its nonnegative Lebesgue integral (the supremum of the integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions bounded above by f). For a set B and constant c≥0, c 1_B is c on B and zero outside B. For a bounded open interval J=(a,b) with a<b its length |J| means b−a.

value.representation_notes: GPEucl k abbreviates EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), inspected in PiL2.lean: EuclideanSpace is PiLp 2, where 2 is the L2 norm exponent, not a dimension; Fin k is the finite coordinate index. EuclideanSpace.dist_eq/dist_sq_eq give the square root of the sum of squared real coordinate distances. WithLp.toLp 2 wraps coordinate functions and Fin.snoc appends the last real coordinate; GPhead uses castSucc and Fin.last k is the final index in Fin(k+1). GPproduct E is exactly the set of vectors whose first n coordinates lie in E and whose last coordinate lies in Icc 0 1; T001 checks its metric and reconstruction identities. No alternative product norm appears. GPcover uses arbitrary countable ℕ-indexed sets, allowing finite covers by empty padding, with Metric.ediam (the supremum of pairwise edists) bounded by ofReal δ. GPcost uses ENNReal real powers and nonnegative extended sums; for s>0 empty/singleton costs are zero and infinite diameters have infinite cost. GPcontent and GPmass are exactly D003's infimum and positive-scale supremum, rather than assuming equality with native measure. T002 proves the native comparison both for Euclidean sets and for the real line used in D006. dimH is the inspected native ENNReal supremum over nonnegative real exponents of infinite native measure; top is infinity, and no toReal truncation of dimension is used. ofReal maps a real to its nonnegative part; all scale/cost-threshold conversions have positivity guards. A comparison dimH A < ofReal q forces q>0, so it is exactly the source real-exponent condition q>dim_H A even when dimH A may be infinite. Finite diameter toReal conversions occur only after GPcover bounds them by finite ofReal δ. At native critical-exponent calls s>0 identifies s.toNNReal with s in both ℝ and ENNReal. Lebesgue integration uses the actual real-line volume and measurable interval indicators; covering sets remain arbitrary. H001-H003 are retained, no M or Audit A note is a premise. All library applications remain proof obligations, not accepted definitions. The inspected ENNReal.tsum_eq_iSup_sum identifies ∑' with the supremum of finite subsums, exactly D002's convention, so no summability assumption is encoded.

steps.statement:
(∀ (k : ℕ) (x : GPEucl k) (t : ℝ),
    GPhead (GPappend x t) = x ∧ (GPappend x t) (Fin.last k) = t) ∧
  (∀ (k : ℕ) (z : GPEucl (k + 1)), GPappend (GPhead z) (z (Fin.last k)) = z) ∧
  (∀ (k : ℕ) (x y : GPEucl k) (t u : ℝ),
    dist (GPappend x t) (GPappend y u) =
      Real.sqrt (dist x y ^ 2 + |t - u| ^ 2)) ∧
  (∀ (k : ℕ) (z w : GPEucl (k + 1)),
    dist (GPhead z) (GPhead w) ≤ dist z w ∧
    |z (Fin.last k) - w (Fin.last k)| ≤ dist z w)
steps.explanation: Implementation geometry for D001/D007: use Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.snoc_last and finite-coordinate extensionality for inverse identities, then EuclideanSpace.dist_sq_eq and the last-coordinate finite-sum split. Prove the two projection contractions from nonnegative squared summands. This is the coordinate calculation already used in the four cited paragraphs; it changes no metric.

steps.statement:
(∀ (k : ℕ) (A : Set (GPEucl k)) (s : ℝ), 0 < s →
    GPmass s A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure s A) ∧
  (∀ (A : Set ℝ) (s : ℝ), 0 < s →
    GPmass s A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure s A)
steps.explanation: Unfold hausdorffMeasure_apply and compare its extended-radius covering infimum with GPcover/GPcost. For positive s the empty-set term is zero, so the nonemptiness supremum can be removed; infinite radius adds no larger value than radius 1. Finite positive extended radii correspond exactly to positive real radii via ofReal/toReal. The same definition comparison on ℝ implements D006's real-line convention without adding a premise or changing the exported N001 domain.

steps.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) (A : Set (GPEucl k)) (s : ℝ), 0 < s →
  GPmass s A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure s A ∧
  0 ≤ dimH A ∧
  (dimH A < ENNReal.ofReal s → GPmass s A = 0) ∧
  (ENNReal.ofReal s < dimH A → GPmass s A = ⊤) ∧
  (GPmass s A = 0 → dimH A ≤ ENNReal.ofReal s) ∧
  (GPmass s A = ⊤ → ENNReal.ofReal s ≤ dimH A) ∧
  (∀ (δ₁ δ₂ : ℝ), 0 < δ₁ → 0 < δ₂ → δ₁ ≤ δ₂ →
    GPcontent s δ₂ A ≤ GPcontent s δ₁ A) ∧
  (GPmass s A = 0 → ∀ (δ ε : ℝ), 0 < δ → 0 < ε →
    ∃ U : ℕ → Set (GPEucl k), GPcover A δ U ∧ GPcost s U < ENNReal.ofReal ε) ∧
  (GPmass s A = ⊤ → ∀ (L δ₀ : ℝ), 0 < L → 0 < δ₀ →
    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ δ ≤ δ₀ ∧ ENNReal.ofReal L < GPcontent s δ A)
steps.explanation: Export all clauses of N001 on Eucl(k). Use the Euclidean part of T002 and the native dimension critical-exponent declarations at the nonnegative real exponent s.toNNReal (s>0 proves the cast identity). Prove scale antitonicity by restricting admissible covers. Zero infimum yields arbitrarily cheap covers; an infinite supremum yields a large scale content, then replace the scale by min(δ,δ₀).

steps.statement:
Bornology.IsBounded E ∧
  (∃ R : ℝ, 0 < R ∧ ∀ x ∈ E, ∀ j : Fin n, -R ≤ x j ∧ x j ≤ R) ∧
  (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ →
  ∃ T : Finset (GPEucl n),
    (E ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ T, Metric.ball x (δ / 2)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ T, Metric.ediam (Metric.ball x (δ / 2)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ) ∧
    (∑ x ∈ T, (Metric.ediam (Metric.ball x (δ / 2))) ^ s) < (⊤ : ENNReal)) ∧
  (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → GPcontent s δ E < ⊤)
steps.explanation: Use IsCompact.isBounded with the actual metric bornology; bound coordinates by the Euclidean norm and enlarge the bound to positive R. Use compactness on the open balls of radius δ/2 to get a finite subcover. The triangle inequality bounds each extended diameter by ofReal δ; a finite sum of these finite positive-exponent costs is finite. Enumerate the finite cover and pad by empty sets when comparing with GPcontent.

steps.statement:
Bornology.IsBounded E ∧
  (∃ R : ℝ, 0 < R ∧ ∀ x ∈ E, ∀ j : Fin n, -R ≤ x j ∧ x j ≤ R) ∧
  (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ →
  ∃ T : Finset (GPEucl n),
    (E ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ T, Metric.ball x (δ / 2)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ T, Metric.ediam (Metric.ball x (δ / 2)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ) ∧
    (∑ x ∈ T, (Metric.ediam (Metric.ball x (δ / 2))) ^ s) < (⊤ : ENNReal)) ∧
  (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → GPcontent s δ E < ⊤) ∧
  (0 ≤ dimH E ∧ dimH E ≤ (n : ENNReal) ∧ dimH E < ⊤) ∧
  (n = 0 → E = Set.univ ∧ E.Subsingleton ∧ dimH E = 0)
steps.explanation: Export N002, retaining T004's boundedness/box/finite-ball-cover and finite-content clauses. For n≥1 use the supplied coordinate grid in the fixed box, count at most C h^(-n) cubes and bound diameter by √n h. tendsto_rpow_neg_atTop at y=s-n proves arbitrarily small cost for s>n. Apply N001 and the strict-between argument to bound dimH E≤n, hence finiteness. If n=0, nonemptiness makes E all of the singleton ambient space, whose positive-exponent costs vanish. No finiteness is assumed.

steps.statement:
∀ (B : Set ℝ) (ρ η : ℝ), B.Nonempty → 0 ≤ ρ →
  (∀ b ∈ B, ∀ b' ∈ B, |b - b'| ≤ ρ) → 0 < η →
  BddAbove B ∧ BddBelow B ∧ IsLUB B (sSup B) ∧ IsGLB B (sInf B) ∧
  sSup B - sInf B ≤ ρ ∧
  B ⊆ Set.Ioo (sInf B - η / 2) (sSup B + η / 2) ∧
  (sInf B - η / 2 < sSup B + η / 2) ∧
  ((sSup B + η / 2) - (sInf B - η / 2) ≤ ρ + η)
steps.explanation: Export N003 with the actual endpoints and their least/greatest-bound properties. A chosen member bounds B on both sides. Real completeness supplies IsLUB/IsGLB, identified with conditional sSup/sInf only after these boundedness conditions. The source order argument proves sup-inf≤ρ, and enlarging by η/2 gives the stated nonempty open interval and length bound, including ρ=0. No measurability of B is used.

steps.statement:
n = 0 →
  dimH (GPproduct E) ≤ dimH E + 1 ∧
  ∀ (q δ : ℝ), dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → 0 < δ →
    GPcontent (q + 1) δ (GPproduct E) = 0 ∧ GPmass (q + 1) (GPproduct E) = 0
steps.explanation: For n=0, N002 identifies E with the singleton and D=0. Append the N equal closed interval pieces, using T001's distance identity. Their maximum diameter is 1/N and their a-cost is N^(1-a), tending to zero for a>1 by tendsto_rpow_neg_atTop. At every scale obtain zero content and mass; N001 gives the dimension upper bound by strict-between.

steps.statement:
1 ≤ n → ∀ (q r ε : ℝ),
  dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → 0 < r → r ≤ 1 → 0 < ε →
  ∃ U : ℕ → Set (GPEucl n),
    GPcover E r U ∧
    (∀ i, (U i).Nonempty → 0 < Metric.ediam (U i)) ∧
    GPcost q U < ENNReal.ofReal ε
steps.explanation: Start with N001's r-cover of q-cost below ε/2. Empty members may be retained as zero-cost padding. A nonempty zero-diameter member is a singleton; replace it by a sufficiently small ball with strictly positive diameter, available because 1≤n, and q-cost less than ε 2^(-i-2). Bound the added cost by the geometric series. Countable choice stays inside this existence statement.

steps.statement:
1 ≤ n → ∀ (q r ε : ℝ),
  dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → 0 < r → r ≤ 1 → 0 < ε →
  ∃ W : ℕ → Set (GPEucl (n + 1)),
    GPcover (GPproduct E) (Real.sqrt 2 * r) W ∧
    GPcost (q + 1) W <
      ENNReal.ofReal (2 * (Real.sqrt 2) ^ (q + 1) * ε)
steps.explanation: Choose T008's U. On nonempty indices, convert finite positive ediam to the real r_i, set N_i=ceil(1/r_i), and partition I into N_i pieces. Form their coordinate-appended cylinders. T001 bounds each diameter by √2 r_i. The ceiling bounds give cost≤2(√2)^(q+1)Σr_i^q, hence the strict displayed estimate. Enumerate the countable dependent index set with empty padding; regroup only nonnegative sums.

steps.statement:
dimH (GPproduct E) ≤ dimH E + 1 ∧
  ∀ (q δ : ℝ), dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → 0 < δ →
    GPcontent (q + 1) δ (GPproduct E) = 0 ∧
    GPmass (q + 1) (GPproduct E) = 0
steps.explanation: Export N004. In positive dimension choose r=min(1,δ/√2) in T009 and make ε arbitrarily small, obtaining zero content at every δ and zero mass for each q>D. Apply N001 to get dimH F≤ofReal(q+1). N002 makes D finite, so a strict-between argument as q↓D proves dimH F≤D+1, also excluding infinite dimH F. Combine with T007 for n=0; do not assert a measure conclusion at q=D.

steps.statement:
∀ (s δ ε : ℝ) (V : ℕ → Set (GPEucl (n + 1))),
  0 < s → 0 < δ → 0 < ε → GPcover (GPproduct E) δ V →
  (∀ i, Metric.ediam (GPhead '' V i) ≤ Metric.ediam (V i)) ∧
  ∃ a b : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ i, (V i).Nonempty →
    a i < b i ∧
    (∀ z ∈ V i, z (Fin.last n) ∈ Set.Ioo (a i) (b i)) ∧
    b i - a i ≤ (Metric.ediam (V i)).toReal +
      ε * (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(i : ℝ) - 1) /
        (1 + (Metric.ediam (V i)).toReal ^ s)
steps.explanation: For each nonempty V_i, T001 gives contraction of the horizontal and vertical projections. GPcover bounds every ediam by the finite ofReal δ, justifying toReal and reconstruction by ofReal. Apply N003 to the vertical image with ρ_i=ediam(V_i).toReal and η_i=ε 2^(-i-1)/(1+ρ_i^s). Choose real endpoints simultaneously on nonempty indices and arbitrary endpoints on empty indices. No projection measurability is introduced.

steps.statement:
∀ (s δ : ℝ) (V : ℕ → Set (GPEucl (n + 1))),
  0 < s → 0 < δ → GPcover (GPproduct E) δ V →
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    GPcontent s δ E ≤ GPcost (s + 1) V + ENNReal.ofReal ε
steps.explanation: Use T011's intervals. For t∈I the horizontal projections with t∈J_i cover E, so their weighted indicator sum bounds c=GPcontent s δ E. The functions ρ_i^s 1_(J_i∩I) are measurable since J_i is open; c is finite by N002. Apply lintegral_mono, lintegral_tsum and lintegral_indicator_const, with volume_Icc=1 and volume_Ioo equal to interval length. Bound the error sum by ε using the chosen η_i and geometric weights. Extended nonnegative sums require no integrability or finite total right-hand cost.

steps.statement:
∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ →
  GPcontent s δ E ≤ GPcontent (s + 1) δ (GPproduct E)
steps.explanation: Export N005. For an arbitrary cover, an infinite cost gives the inequality immediately; otherwise T012 and finiteness of c allow ε↓0. Empty members have zero cost because s+1>0. Take the infimum over all admissible covers, retaining arbitrary nonmeasurable covers.

steps.statement: dimH GPI ≤ 1 ∧ ∀ a : ℝ, 1 < a → GPmass a GPI = 0
steps.explanation: Divide the real interval into N equal closed pieces. At every fixed scale, N large gives an admissible cover of a-cost N^(1-a)→0 for a>1. Hence GPmass a GPI=0. Use T002's real-line equality and the native dimension critical-exponent theorem, then the strict-between argument to obtain dimH GPI≤1. This is D006's usual real metric; no supremum product norm is used.

steps.statement:
∀ (δ : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set ℝ), 0 < δ →
  GPcover GPI δ U → (1 : ENNReal) ≤ ∑' i, Metric.ediam (U i)
steps.explanation: Enclose the nonempty members of U in N003's open intervals of length≤ρ_i+ε 2^(-i-1). Finite scale bounds justify the real diameters. The intervals cover I, so volume_Icc, volume_Ioo, monotonicity and measure_iUnion_le give 1≤Σρ_i+ε. Remove ε, considering infinite and finite sums separately. Empty members contribute zero.

steps.statement:
dimH GPI = 1 ∧
  ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s < 1 → GPmass s GPI = ⊤
steps.explanation: For 0<s<1 and δ>0, use ρ^s≥δ^(s-1)ρ for 0≤ρ≤δ, treating ρ=0 separately. T015 implies GPcontent s δ GPI≥ofReal(δ^(s-1)). tendsto_rpow_neg_nhdsGT_zero at s-1<0 makes the mass infinite. T002 transfers this to native real Hausdorff measure; native le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_eq_top and the strict-between argument yield dimH GPI≥1. Combine with T014.

steps.statement:
dimH GPI = 1 ∧
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s < 1 → GPmass s GPI = ⊤) ∧
  (∀ (k : ℕ) (A : Set (GPEucl k)) (e : GPI → GPEucl k),
    (∀ t, e t ∈ A) →
    (∀ t u, dist (e t) (e u) = |(t : ℝ) - (u : ℝ)|) →
    (1 : ENNReal) ≤ dimH A ∧
    ∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ →
      GPcontent s δ GPI ≤ GPcontent s δ A)
steps.explanation: Export N006, retaining T016's interval clauses. Pull an arbitrary δ-cover V of A back along e to P_i={t∈I:e(t)∈V_i}; the subtype domain makes all values of e lie in I's intended domain. Distance preservation gives ediam(P_i)≤ediam(V_i), so compare costs and then infima to obtain the content inequality for every positive s,δ. import Mathlib
abbrev GPEucl (k : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)
def GPI : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
def GPappend {k : ℕ} (x : GPEucl k) (t : ℝ) : GPEucl (k + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => x i) t)
def GPhead {k : ℕ} (z : GPEucl (k + 1)) : GPEucl k :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin k => z i.castSucc)
def GPproduct {k : ℕ} (A : Set (GPEucl k)) : Set (GPEucl (k + 1)) :=
  {z | GPhead z ∈ A ∧ z (Fin.last k) ∈ GPI}
def GPcover {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
    (A : Set X) (δ : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
noncomputable def GPcost {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X) : ENNReal :=
  ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
noncomputable def GPcontent {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
    (s δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ENNReal :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : GPcover A δ U), GPcost s U
noncomputable def GPmass {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ENNReal :=
  ⨆ (δ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < δ), GPcontent s δ A

EuclideanSpace.dist_eq/dist_sq_eq give the square root of the sum of squared real coordinate distances. WithLp.toLp 2 wraps coordinate functions and Fin.snoc appends the last real coordinate; GPhead uses castSucc and Fin.last k is the final index in Fin(k+1). GPproduct E is exactly the set of vectors whose first n coordinates lie in E and whose last coordinate lies in Icc 0 1; T001 checks its metric and reconstruction identities. No alternative product norm appears. GPcover uses arbitrary countable ℕ-indexed sets, allowing finite covers by empty padding, with Metric.ediam (the supremum of pairwise edists) bounded by ofReal δ. GPcost uses ENNReal real powers and nonnegative extended sums; for s>0 empty/singleton costs are zero and infinite diameters have infinite cost. GPcontent and GPmass are exactly D003's infimum and positive-scale supremum, rather than assuming equality with native measure. T002 proves the native comparison both for Euclidean sets and for the real line used in D006. dimH is the inspected native ENNReal supremum over nonnegative real exponents of infinite native measure; top is infinity, and no toReal truncation of dimension is used. ofReal maps a real to its nonnegative part; all scale/cost-threshold conversions have positivity guards. Thus the inner infimum is precisely H^s_r(A). The radius ∞ contributes no larger value than the radius 1, since every cover admissible at 1 is admissible at ∞. Hence allowing extended radii does not enlarge the supremum over finite positive radii. Finite or other countable covers can be enumerated and padded by empty members, preserving every cost. M001 therefore gives H^s(A)=Native(Eucl(k)).measure(s)(A).

The dimension in D005 is exactly the native dimension, and is nonnegative since it takes values in [0,∞]. Under s>0, s defines a nonnegative real source exponent. Apply M002 when s<dim_H(A) to obtain native measure ∞, and apply M003 when dim_H(A)<s to obtain native measure zero. In both cases F001 identifies this value with H^s(A). If H^s(A)=0, F001 makes the native measure different from ∞, so M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s. If H^s(A)=∞, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A). Each conditional source use retains exactly its antecedent; no conclusion is asserted without that antecedent.

For positive δ, decreasing δ restricts the admissible covers and therefore increases their infimum. All costs are nonnegative. If H^s(A)=0, every scale infimum is zero. By the defining greatest-lower-bound property, for every positive threshold a cover has cost below it: otherwise that positive threshold would be a lower bound. If H^s(A)=∞, its defining supremum supplies a scale with content>L for every finite L>0. Replacing that scale by its minimum with δ0 preserves this strict inequality and gives a scale no larger than δ0. These are implications for arbitrary positive L,δ0,δ. Discharge L1 and universally quantify k,A,s with its positivity condition, obtaining the exported conclusion.

H002 and M012 imply that E is bounded in the Euclidean metric bornology. In Euclidean space, a bounded set has its distances from the origin bounded by a finite constant; increasing that bound to a positive number bounds each absolute coordinate of every x∈E, because for every coordinate j<n, |x_j|≤(∑_{j<n}|x_j|^2)^(1/2). Thus there exists R>0 such that E⊆[−R,R]^n. This interpretation uses precisely the metric bornology, whose bounded sets lie in some finite-radius ball.

Choose R from F001. For arbitrary s>0,δ>0, cover E by the open balls of radius δ/2 centered at every point of Eucl(n). They cover since each point belongs to its own ball. Each ball is open in D001's metric topology, and its diameter is≤δ by the triangle inequality. H002 and M013 supply a finite subcover. Thus a finite ball-cover with these diameters exists for every positive δ.

For each positive s and δ in F002, choose its finite subcover T. Each ball's s-cost is≤δ^s, so the finite cost sum is finite. The infimum H^s_δ(E) is no greater than that cost, and is therefore finite. This proves the universally quantified finite-cover and content clauses in the exported conclusion.

First assume L1: n≥1. For 0<h≤1 partition each coordinate interval [−R,R] into at most ceil(2R/h) closed subintervals of length≤h. Their products cover the box and hence E. The number of cubes (possibly shorter at the boundary) is≤(2R/h+1)^n≤C h^(−n), where C=(2R+1)^n depends only on the fixed box. Each diameter is≤√n h by summing the squared coordinate differences. For s>n the total s-cost is≤C n^(s/2) h^(s−n), which tends to zero as h↓0 by M015 with y=s−n>0 and source variable 1/h; the factor C n^(s/2) is fixed and finite. For any fixed target scale, h can be arbitrarily small while √n h is below it; hence every scale content is zero and H^s(E)=0. N001 gives D≤s for every s>n. It follows that D≤n: if D>n, choose a finite real s strictly between n and D (also possible if D=∞), contradicting D≤s. Discharge L1. In the case L1: n=0, N002 gives E=Eucl(0), a singleton, and D=0. The coordinate map t↦((),t) preserves Euclidean distances by D001. 1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.
168: 
169: ## Input status
170:

172: tests. It is a natural-language input, not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
173: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must independently produce
174: and check those artifacts. The basic Hausdorff-measure and integration facts
175: used here must be registered by that future NL0/Audit A workflow.

1: import Mathlib
2: abbrev GPEucl (k : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)
3: def GPI : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
4: def GPappend {k : ℕ} (x : GPEucl k) (t : ℝ) : GPEucl (k + 1) :=
5:   WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => x i) t)
6: def GPhead {k : ℕ} (z : GPEucl (k + 1)) : GPEucl k :=
7:   WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin k => z i.castSucc)
8: def GPproduct {k : ℕ} (A : Set (GPEucl k)) : Set (GPEucl (k + 1)) :=
9:   {z | GPhead z ∈ A ∧ z (Fin.last k) ∈ GPI}
10: def GPcover {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
11:     (A : Set X) (δ : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
12:   A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
13: noncomputable def GPcost {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
14:     (s : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X) : ENNReal :=
15:   ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
16: noncomputable def GPcontent {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
17:     (s δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ENNReal :=
18:   ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : GPcover A δ U), GPcost s U
19: noncomputable def GPmass {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
20:     (s : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ENNReal :=
21:   ⨆ (δ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < δ), GPcontent s δ A

1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
4: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
5: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
6: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
7: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
8: 
9: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
10: 
11: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
12: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
13: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
14: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
15: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
16: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
17: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
18: 
19: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
20: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
21: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
22: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
23: 
24: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
25: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
26: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
27: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
28: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
29: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
30: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
31: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
32: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
33: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
34: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
35: 
36: ## Author correspondence explanations
37: 
38: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
39: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
40: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
41: line-by-line formalization commentary:
42: 
43: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
44:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
45: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
46:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
47:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
48: 
49: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
50: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
51: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
52: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
53: 
54: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
55: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
56: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
57: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
58: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
59: 
60: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
61: 
62: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
63: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
64: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
65: row, then these four global checks:
66: 
67: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
68:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
69: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
70:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
71:    no external inputs, record that fact.
72: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
73:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
74:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
75: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
76:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
77:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
78: 
79: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
80: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
81: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
82: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
83: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
84: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
85: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
86: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
87: 
88: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
89: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
90: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
91: 
92: ## Freely available Mathlib
93: 
94: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
95: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
96: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
97: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
98: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
99: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
100: permissions to use a library theorem.
101: 
102: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
103: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
104: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
105: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
106: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
107: require returning to the affected source boundary.
108: 
109: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
110: 
111: ### Compact review materials
112: 
113: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
114: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
115: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
116: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
117: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
118: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
119: expected type for the actual inspected type.
120: 
121: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
122: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
123: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
124: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
125: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
126: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
127: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
128: 
129: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
130: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
131: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
132: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
133: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
134: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
135: 
136: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
137: 
138: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
139: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
140: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
141: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
142: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
143: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
144: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
145: 
146: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
147: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
148: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
149: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
150: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
151: 
152: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
153: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
154: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
155: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
156: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
157: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
158: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
159: 
160: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
161: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
162: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
163: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
164: review have separate recorded outcomes.
165: 
166: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
167: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
168: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
169: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
170: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
171: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
172: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
173: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
174: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
175: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs.

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 300 seconds, and use Lean's finite default heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and independent endpoint-fidelity Audit B remain required.

1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150:

Fix an arbitrary A⊆Eucl(k).
Fix an arbitrary real s; for the following conditional argument assume s>0.
Let δ>0 be arbitrary, locally under the positive-scale condition.

At each finite positive radius r consider any countable cover U admissible at r.
Let U be an arbitrary admissible r-cover in the inner infimum.

argument.text: Fix k,A,s as declared and temporarily assume L1: s>0. Apply M001 to X=Eucl(k), σ=s and the current A. Its Borel structure is the one fixed in D001. At a finite positive radius the summand for an empty member is zero and that for a nonempty member is (diam U_i)^s; this also vanishes on a singleton because s>0. Thus the inner infimum is precisely H^s_r(A). The radius ∞ contributes no larger value than the radius 1, since every cover admissible at 1 is admissible at ∞. Hence allowing extended radii does not enlarge the supremum over finite positive radii. Finite or other countable covers can be enumerated and padded by empty members, preserving every cost. M001 therefore gives H^s(A)=Native(Eucl(k)).measure(s)(A).

produces.statement: H^s(A)=Native(Eucl(k)).measure(s)(A).

argument.text: The dimension in D005 is exactly the native dimension, and is nonnegative since it takes values in [0,∞]. Under s>0, s defines a nonnegative real source exponent. Apply M002 when s<dim_H(A) to obtain native measure ∞, and apply M003 when dim_H(A)<s to obtain native measure zero. In both cases F001 identifies this value with H^s(A). If H^s(A)=0, F001 makes the native measure different from ∞, so M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s. If H^s(A)=∞, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A). Each conditional source use retains exactly its antecedent; no conclusion is asserted without that antecedent.

produces.statement: dim_H(A)≥0; if s>dim_H(A) then H^s(A)=0; if 0<s<dim_H(A) then H^s(A)=∞; if H^s(A)=0 then dim_H(A)≤s; and if H^s(A)=∞ then dim_H(A)≥s.

argument.text: For positive δ, decreasing δ restricts the admissible covers and therefore increases their infimum. All costs are nonnegative. If H^s(A)=0, every scale infimum is zero. By the defining greatest-lower-bound property, for every positive threshold a cover has cost below it: otherwise that positive threshold would be a lower bound. If H^s(A)=∞, its defining supremum supplies a scale with content>L for every finite L>0. Replacing that scale by its minimum with δ0 preserves this strict inequality and gives a scale no larger than δ0. These are implications for arbitrary positive L,δ0,δ. Discharge L1 and universally quantify k,A,s with its positivity condition, obtaining the exported conclusion.

locals.declaration: Choose R>0 with E⊆[−R,R]^n, whose existence was established in F001.

locals.type: finite set of centers in Eucl(n)
locals.declaration: At the current positive δ, choose the finite centers T whose radius-δ/2 balls cover E, supplied by F002.
Fix an arbitrary 0<h≤1 in the mesh argument.
Define C=(2R+1)^n, independent of h.
For the coordinate bound let x be any point of E.

argument.text: H002 and M012 imply that E is bounded in the Euclidean metric bornology. In Euclidean space, a bounded set has its distances from the origin bounded by a finite constant; increasing that bound to a positive number bounds each absolute coordinate of every x∈E, because for every coordinate j<n, |x_j|≤(∑_{j<n}|x_j|^2)^(1/2). Thus there exists R>0 such that E⊆[−R,R]^n. This interpretation uses precisely the metric bornology, whose bounded sets lie in some finite-radius ball.

produces.statement: There exists R′>0 with E⊆[−R′,R′]^n.

argument.text: Choose R from F001. For arbitrary s>0,δ>0, cover E by the open balls of radius δ/2 centered at every point of Eucl(n). They cover since each point belongs to its own ball. Each ball is open in D001's metric topology, and its diameter is≤δ by the triangle inequality. H002 and M013 supply a finite subcover. Thus a finite ball-cover with these diameters exists for every positive δ.

produces.statement: For every δ′>0 there is a finite set T′⊆Eucl(n) such that the balls with centers in T′ and radius δ′/2 cover E and have diameter≤δ′.

argument.text: For each positive s and δ in F002, choose its finite subcover T. Each ball's s-cost is≤δ^s, so the finite cost sum is finite. The infimum H^s_δ(E) is no greater than that cost, and is therefore finite. This proves the universally quantified finite-cover and content clauses in the exported conclusion.

produces.statement: For every s′>0 and δ′>0, E has a finite ball-cover of diameter≤δ′ with finite total s′-cost, and H^s′_δ′(E)<∞.

argument.text: First assume L1: n≥1. For 0<h≤1 partition each coordinate interval [−R,R] into at most ceil(2R/h) closed subintervals of length≤h. Their products cover the box and hence E. The number of cubes (possibly shorter at the boundary) is≤(2R/h+1)^n≤C h^(−n), where C=(2R+1)^n depends only on the fixed box. Each diameter is≤√n h by summing the squared coordinate differences. For s>n the total s-cost is≤C n^(s/2) h^(s−n), which tends to zero as h↓0 by M015 with y=s−n>0 and source variable 1/h; the factor C n^(s/2) is fixed and finite. For any fixed target scale, h can be arbitrarily small while √n h is below it; hence every scale content is zero and H^s(E)=0. N001 gives D≤s for every s>n. It follows that D≤n: if D>n, choose a finite real s strictly between n and D (also possible if D=∞), contradicting D≤s. Discharge L1. In the remaining case L2: n=0, Eucl(0) has only the empty vector; H001 implies E=Eucl(0). Its singleton cover has zero s-cost for every s>0, so N001 gives D≤s for every positive s, whence D=0. Discharge L2. Nonnegativity in both cases is N001, giving 0≤D≤n and all the remaining clauses of the exported conclusion.

result.text:
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.

1: import Mathlib
2: abbrev GPEucl (k : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)
3: def GPI : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
4: def GPappend {k : ℕ} (x : GPEucl k) (t : ℝ) : GPEucl (k + 1) :=
5:   WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => x i) t)
6: def GPhead {k : ℕ} (z : GPEucl (k + 1)) : GPEucl k :=
7:   WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin k => z i.castSucc)
8: def GPproduct {k : ℕ} (A : Set (GPEucl k)) : Set (GPEucl (k + 1)) :=
9:   {z | GPhead z ∈ A ∧ z (Fin.last k) ∈ GPI}
10: def GPcover {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
11:     (A : Set X) (δ : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
12:   A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
13: noncomputable def GPcost {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
14:     (s : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X) : ENNReal :=
15:   ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
16: noncomputable def GPcontent {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
17:     (s δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ENNReal :=
18:   ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : GPcover A δ U), GPcost s U
19: noncomputable def GPmass {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
20:     (s : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ENNReal :=
21:   ⨆ (δ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < δ), GPcontent s δ A

96: /-- Hausdorff dimension of a set in an (e)metric space. -/
97: @[irreducible] noncomputable def dimH (s : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ := by
98:   borelize X; exact ⨆ (d : ℝ≥0) (_ : @hausdorffMeasure X _ _ ⟨rfl⟩ d s = ∞), d

109: /-- Unfold the definition of `dimH` using `[MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]` from the
110: environment. -/
111: theorem dimH_def (s : Set X) : dimH s = ⨆ (d : ℝ≥0) (_ : μH[d] s = ∞), (d : ℝ≥0∞) := by
112:   borelize X; rw [dimH]

114: theorem hausdorffMeasure_of_lt_dimH {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : ↑d < dimH s) : μH[d] s = ∞ := by
115:   simp only [dimH_def, lt_iSup_iff] at h
116:   rcases h with ⟨d', hsd', hdd'⟩
117:   rw [ENNReal.coe_lt_coe, ← NNReal.coe_lt_coe] at hdd'
118:   exact top_unique (hsd' ▸ hausdorffMeasure_mono hdd'.le _)

124:   le_of_not_gt <| mt hausdorffMeasure_of_lt_dimH h

126: theorem le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_eq_top {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : μH[d] s = ∞) :
127:     ↑d ≤ dimH s := by
128:   rw [dimH_def]; exact le_iSup₂ (α := ℝ≥0∞) d h
129: 
130: theorem hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : dimH s < d) : μH[d] s = 0 := by
131:   rw [dimH_def] at h

133:   rw [ENNReal.coe_lt_coe, ← NNReal.coe_lt_coe] at hd'd
134:   exact (hausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top hd'd s).resolve_right fun h₂ => hsd'.not_ge <|
135:     le_iSup₂ (α := ℝ≥0∞) d' h₂
136:

138:     (hd : dimH s < d) : μ s = 0 :=
139:   h <| hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt hd
140: 
141: theorem le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : μH[d] s ≠ 0) : ↑d ≤ dimH s :=
142:   le_of_not_gt <| mt hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt h

148: /-- The Hausdorff dimension of a set `s` is the infimum of all `d : ℝ≥0` such that the
149: `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of `s` is zero. This infimum is taken in `ℝ≥0∞`.

155:     intro i hi j hj

128: ### Metric outer measures
129: 
130: In this section we define metric outer measures and prove Carathéodory's theorem: a metric outer
131: measure has the Carathéodory property.
132: -/

135: /-- We say that an outer measure `μ` in an (e)metric space is *metric* if `μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t`
136: for any two metric separated sets `s`, `t`. -/
137: def IsMetric (μ : OuterMeasure X) : Prop :=
138:   ∀ s t : Set X, Metric.AreSeparated s t → μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t
139: 
140: namespace IsMetric
141: 
142: variable {μ : OuterMeasure X}
143: 
144: /-- A metric outer measure is additive on a finite set of pairwise metric separated sets. -/
145: theorem finset_iUnion_of_pairwise_separated (hm : IsMetric μ) {I : Finset ι} {s : ι → Set X}
146:     (hI : ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j ∈ I, i ≠ j → Metric.AreSeparated (s i) (s j)) :
147:     μ (⋃ i ∈ I, s i) = ∑ i ∈ I, μ (s i) := by
148:   classical
149:   induction I using Finset.induction_on with
150:   | empty => simp
151:   | insert i I hiI ihI =>
152:     simp only [Finset.mem_insert] at hI
153:     rw [Finset.set_biUnion_insert, hm, ihI, Finset.sum_insert hiI]
154:     exacts [fun i hi j hj hij => hI i (Or.inr hi) j (Or.inr hj) hij,
155:       Metric.AreSeparated.finset_iUnion_right fun j hj =>
156:         hI i (Or.inl rfl) j (Or.inr hj) (ne_of_mem_of_not_mem hj hiI).symm]
157: 
158: /-- **Carathéodory's theorem**. If `m` is a metric outer measure, then every Borel measurable set
159: `t` is Carathéodory measurable: for any (not necessarily measurable) set `s` we have
160: `μ (s ∩ t) + μ (s \ t) = μ s`. -/
161: theorem borel_le_caratheodory (hm : IsMetric μ) : borel X ≤ μ.caratheodory := by
162:   rw [borel_eq_generateFrom_isClosed]
163:   refine MeasurableSpace.generateFrom_le fun t ht => μ.isCaratheodory_iff_le.2 fun s => ?_
164:   set S : ℕ → Set X := fun n => {x ∈ s | (↑n)⁻¹ ≤ infEDist x t}
165:   have Ssep (n) : Metric.AreSeparated (S n) t :=
166:     ⟨n⁻¹, ENNReal.inv_ne_zero.2 (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top _),
167:       fun x hx y hy ↦ hx.2.trans <| infEDist_le_edist_of_mem hy⟩
168:   have Ssep' : ∀ n, Metric.AreSeparated (S n) (s ∩ t) := fun n =>
169:     (Ssep n).mono Subset.rfl inter_subset_right
170:   have S_sub : ∀ n, S n ⊆ s \ t := fun n =>
171:     subset_inter inter_subset_left (Ssep n).subset_compl_right
172:   have hSs : ∀ n, μ (s ∩ t) + μ (S n) ≤ μ s := fun n =>
173:     calc
174:       μ (s ∩ t) + μ (S n) = μ (s ∩ t ∪ S n) := Eq.symm <| hm _ _ <| (Ssep' n).symm
175:       _ ≤ μ (s ∩ t ∪ s \ t) := μ.mono <| union_subset_union_right _ <| S_sub n
176:       _ = μ s := by rw [inter_union_sdiff]
177:   have iUnion_S : ⋃ n, S n = s \ t := by
178:     refine Subset.antisymm (iUnion_subset S_sub) ?_
179:     rintro x ⟨hxs, hxt⟩
180:     rw [mem_iff_infEDist_zero_of_closed ht] at hxt
181:     rcases ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt hxt with ⟨n, hn⟩
182:     exact mem_iUnion.2 ⟨n, hxs, hn.le⟩
183:   /- Now we have `∀ n, μ (s ∩ t) + μ (S n) ≤ μ s` and we need to prove
184:     `μ (s ∩ t) + μ (⋃ n, S n) ≤ μ s`. We can't pass to the limit because
185:     `μ` is only an outer measure. -/
186:   by_cases htop : μ (s \ t) = ∞
187:   · rw [htop, add_top, ← htop]
188:     exact μ.mono sdiff_subset
189:   suffices μ (⋃ n, S n) ≤ ⨆ n, μ (S n) by calc
190:     μ (s ∩ t) + μ (s \ t) = μ (s ∩ t) + μ (⋃ n, S n) := by rw [iUnion_S]
191:     _ ≤ μ (s ∩ t) + ⨆ n, μ (S n) := by gcongr
192:     _ = ⨆ n, μ (s ∩ t) + μ (S n) := ENNReal.add_iSup ..
193:     _ ≤ μ s := iSup_le hSs
194:   /- It suffices to show that `∑' k, μ (S (k + 1) \ S k) ≠ ∞`. Indeed, if we have this,
195:     then for all `N` we have `μ (⋃ n, S n) ≤ μ (S N) + ∑' k, m (S (N + k + 1) \ S (N + k))`
196:     and the second term tends to zero, see `OuterMeasure.iUnion_nat_of_monotone_of_tsum_ne_top`
197:     for details. -/
198:   have : ∀ n, S n ⊆ S (n + 1) := fun n x hx =>
199:     ⟨hx.1, le_trans (ENNReal.inv_le_inv.2 <| Nat.cast_le.2 n.le_succ) hx.2⟩
200:   refine (μ.iUnion_nat_of_monotone_of_tsum_ne_top this ?_).le; clear this
201:   /- While the sets `S (k + 1) \ S k` are not pairwise metric separated, the sets in each
202:     subsequence `S (2 * k + 1) \ S (2 * k)` and `S (2 * k + 2) \ S (2 * k)` are metric separated,
203:     so `m` is additive on each of those sequences. -/
204:   rw [← tsum_even_add_odd ENNReal.summable ENNReal.summable, ENNReal.add_ne_top]
205:   suffices ∀ a, (∑' k : ℕ, μ (S (2 * k + 1 + a) \ S (2 * k + a))) ≠ ∞ from
206:     ⟨by simpa using this 0, by simpa using this 1⟩
207:   refine fun r => ne_top_of_le_ne_top htop ?_
208:   rw [← iUnion_S, ENNReal.tsum_eq_iSup_nat, iSup_le_iff]
209:   intro n

value.text: Fix k,A,s as declared and temporarily assume L1: s>0. Apply M001 to X=Eucl(k), σ=s and the current A. Its Borel structure is the one fixed in D001. At a finite positive radius the summand for an empty member is zero and that for a nonempty member is (diam U_i)^s; this also vanishes on a singleton because s>0. Thus the inner infimum is precisely H^s_r(A). The radius ∞ contributes no larger value than the radius 1, since every cover admissible at 1 is admissible at ∞. Hence allowing extended radii does not enlarge the supremum over finite positive radii. Finite or other countable covers can be enumerated and padded by empty members, preserving every cost. M001 therefore gives H^s(A)=Native(Eucl(k)).measure(s)(A).

The dimension in D005 is exactly the native dimension, and is nonnegative since it takes values in [0,∞]. Under s>0, s defines a nonnegative real source exponent. Apply M002 when s<dim_H(A) to obtain native measure ∞, and apply M003 when dim_H(A)<s to obtain native measure zero. In both cases F001 identifies this value with H^s(A). If H^s(A)=0, F001 makes the native measure different from ∞, so M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s. If H^s(A)=∞, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A). Each conditional source use retains exactly its antecedent; no conclusion is asserted without that antecedent.

For positive δ, decreasing δ restricts the admissible covers and therefore increases their infimum. All costs are nonnegative. If H^s(A)=0, every scale infimum is zero. By the defining greatest-lower-bound property, for every positive threshold a cover has cost below it: otherwise that positive threshold would be a lower bound. If H^s(A)=∞, its defining supremum supplies a scale with content>L for every finite L>0. Replacing that scale by its minimum with δ0 preserves this strict inequality and gives a scale no larger than δ0. These are implications for arbitrary positive L,δ0,δ. Discharge L1 and universally quantify k,A,s with its positivity condition, obtaining the exported conclusion.

H002 and M012 imply that E is bounded in the Euclidean metric bornology. In Euclidean space, a bounded set has its distances from the origin bounded by a finite constant; increasing that bound to a positive number bounds each absolute coordinate of every x∈E, because for every coordinate j<n, |x_j|≤(∑_{j<n}|x_j|^2)^(1/2). Thus there exists R>0 such that E⊆[−R,R]^n. This interpretation uses precisely the metric bornology, whose bounded sets lie in some finite-radius ball.

Choose R from F001. For arbitrary s>0,δ>0, cover E by the open balls of radius δ/2 centered at every point of Eucl(n). They cover since each point belongs to its own ball. Each ball is open in D001's metric topology, and its diameter is≤δ by the triangle inequality. H002 and M013 supply a finite subcover. Thus a finite ball-cover with these diameters exists for every positive δ.

For each positive s and δ in F002, choose its finite subcover T. Each ball's s-cost is≤δ^s, so the finite cost sum is finite. argument.text: H002 and M012 imply that E is bounded in the Euclidean metric bornology. argument.text: Choose R from F001. For arbitrary s>0,δ>0, cover E by the open balls of radius δ/2 centered at every point of Eucl(n). They cover since each point belongs to its own ball. argument.text: First assume L1: n≥1. For 0<h≤1 partition each coordinate interval [−R,R] into at most ceil(2R/h) closed subintervals of length≤h. Their products cover the box and hence E. The number of cubes (possibly shorter at the boundary) is≤(2R/h+1)^n≤C h^(−n), where C=(2R+1)^n depends only on the fixed box. Each diameter is≤√n h by summing the squared coordinate differences. For s>n the total s-cost is≤C n^(s/2) h^(s−n), which tends to zero as h↓0 by M015 with y=s−n>0 and source variable 1/h; the factor C n^(s/2) is fixed and finite. It follows that D≤n: if D>n, choose a finite real s strictly between n and D (also possible if D=∞), contradicting D≤s. Discharge L1.
